title: Rigveda 1.137: To Mitra and Varuna
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 1.137: To Mitra and Varuna: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 1.137 is a hymn of 3 verses addressed to Mitra and Varuna. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 1, a collection of hymns by many families of poets. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 107r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 1.137.1-3 (aṣṭaka 2, adhyāya 2, varga 1); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 107r
translation.original_text:
1su̱ṣu̱mā yā̍ta̱m adri̍bhi̱r gośrī̍tā matsa̱rā i̱me somā̍so matsa̱rā i̱me | ā rā̍jānā divispṛśāsma̱trā ga̍nta̱m upa̍ naḥ | i̱me vā̍m mitrāvaruṇā̱ gavā̍śira̱ḥ somā̍ḥ śu̱krā gavā̍śiraḥ ||
2i̱ma ā yā̍ta̱m inda̍va̱ḥ somā̍so̱ dadhyā̍śiraḥ su̱tāso̱ dadhyā̍śiraḥ | u̱ta vā̍m u̱ṣaso̍ bu̱dhi sā̱kaṁ sūrya̍sya ra̱śmibhi̍ḥ | su̱to mi̱trāya̱ varu̍ṇāya pī̱taye̱ cāru̍r ṛ̱tāya̍ pī̱taye̍ ||
3tāṁ vā̍ṁ dhe̱nuṁ na vā̍sa̱rīm a̱ṁśuṁ du̍ha̱nty adri̍bhi̱ḥ soma̍ṁ duha̱nty adri̍bhiḥ | a̱sma̱trā ga̍nta̱m upa̍ no̱ 'rvāñcā̱ soma̍pītaye | a̱yaṁ vā̍m mitrāvaruṇā̱ nṛbhi̍ḥ su̱taḥ soma̱ ā pī̱taye̍ su̱taḥ ||
translation.text:
1WITH stones have we pressed out: O come; these gladdening drops are blent with milk, these Soma-drops which gladden you. Come to us, Kings who reach to heaven, approach us, coming hitherward. These milky drops are yours, Mitra and Varuṇa, bright Soma juices blent with milk.
2Here are the droppings; come ye nigh the Soma-droppings blent with curd, juices expressed and blent with curd. Now for the wakening of your Dawn together with the Sun-God's rays, juice waits for Mitra and for Varuṇa to drink, fair juice for drink, for sacrihce.
3As 'twere a radiant-coloured cow, they milk with stones the stalk for you, with stones they milk the Soma-plant. May ye come nigh us, may ye turn hither to drink the Soma juice. The men pressed out this juice, Mitra and Varuṇa, pressed out this Soma for your drink.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 107r (numbered 1r by the scribe) (OPenn image 108, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 1.137.1 ‹suṣuma ā yātam adri-bhiḥ›. Line 1 opens with hariḥ oṃ, then 1.137.1 (susuma ā yātam adribhiḥ); the last line of fol. 106v has the colophon of aṣṭaka 2, adhyāya 1. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 107v (numbered 1v by the scribe), begins in RV 1.138.1 ‹āyuyuve makhaḥ›. Verses 1.137.1-3 end on this page.
